1	# Product brief
2	
3	## Request
4	    Last Seat: a seat reservation service with expiring holds. A user can hold a seat for a limited time, then confirm it, cancel it or let it expire. One seat is never sold twice, and every hold is eventually released.
5	
6	## Outcomes
7	-     A booker holds a free seat and sees the seat reported as held for them until a stated deadline.
8	-     A booker confirms their held seat before the deadline and sees the seat reported as sold to them.
9	-     A booker cancels their hold and sees the seat reported as free again.
10	-     A booker who does nothing has their hold released automatically at the deadline, and the seat is reported as free again.
11	-     A second booker is refused a seat that is held or sold, so one seat is never sold twice.
12	-     Open: no business motivation was supplied in the Request; the benefit behind these outcomes is not yet stated.
13	
14	## Scope
15	
16	### In scope
17	-     A tiny HTTP API as the public port for every operation and every observation.
18	-     Hold one named seat from a fixed seat inventory for a limited time.
19	-     Confirm a held seat before its deadline.
20	-     Cancel a held seat before its deadline.
21	-     Release a hold automatically when its deadline passes.
22	-     Report every seat as free, held (with holder reference and deadline) or sold.
23	-     Refuse any hold or confirmation that would sell one seat twice.
24	-     A clearly marked demo-only HTTP operation that advances the clock, so expiry is observable during the workshop.
25	-     A single event with one seating area, loaded at start.
26	
27	### Out of scope
28	Applicability: applicable
29	Reason:     The Request names only hold, confirm, cancel and expire for one seat, and the work must stay small enough to deliver live.
30	-     Payment, pricing and refunds.
31	-     User accounts, login and roles.
32	-     Waitlists and any fairness guarantee about who gets a released seat.
33	-     Seat maps and any graphical or web user interface, including the Svelte client the human mentioned.
34	-     Multiple events, venues or seating areas.
35	-     Notifications to the booker.
36	-     Storage that survives a process restart.
37	-     Extension or renewal of a hold.
38	-     Organizer or administrator override of another person's hold.
39	
40	## Jobs to be done
41	
42	### Human
43	- [proposed] When I have found the seat I want, I want to keep it for a short time before I commit, so I can decide without losing the seat to someone else.
44	- [proposed] When I am ready, I want to confirm that the seat is mine, so I can be certain nobody else receives the same seat.
45	- [proposed] When a seat is no longer wanted, I want it to return to the pool quickly, so the seat is not blocked by somebody who walked away.
46	
47	### LLM
48	_Not explored._
49	
50	## User journey
51	
52	| Step | Human emotion | Status |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| The booker asks the HTTP API for the seats and sees which seats are free. | not explored | proposed |
55	| The booker holds one free seat and receives a hold reference and a deadline. | not explored | proposed |
56	| The booker decides while the hold is active; other bookers are refused that seat. | not explored | proposed |
57	| The booker confirms the seat before the deadline, and the seat becomes sold to them. | not explored | proposed |
58	| Or the booker cancels, and the seat becomes free at once. | not explored | proposed |
59	| Or the booker does nothing, and the hold is released at the deadline, so the seat becomes free again. | not explored | proposed |
60	
61	Qualitative journey arc (stated emotions; NOT measured intensity)
62	```text
63	[proposed] 1. The booker asks the HTTP API for the seats and sees which seats are free.
64	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
65	    |
66	    v
67	[proposed] 2. The booker holds one free seat and receives a hold reference and a deadline.
68	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
69	    |
70	    v
71	[proposed] 3. The booker decides while the hold is active; other bookers are refused that seat.
72	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
73	    |
74	    v
75	[proposed] 4. The booker confirms the seat before the deadline, and the seat becomes sold to them.
76	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
77	    |
78	    v
79	[proposed] 5. Or the booker cancels, and the seat becomes free at once.
80	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
81	    |
82	    v
83	[proposed] 6. Or the booker does nothing, and the hold is released at the deadline, so the seat becomes free again.
84	    emotion: UNKNOWN (not explored)
85	```
86	
87	## Gherkin scenarios
88	
89	### A booker holds a free seat (proposed)
90	```gherkin
91	Given seat 12 is free
92	When booker A sends an HTTP request to hold seat 12
93	Then the response gives booker A a hold reference and a deadline
94	And seat 12 is reported as held for booker A
95	```
96	
97	### The last seat is not given to a second booker (proposed)
98	```gherkin
99	Given seat 12 is held for booker A
100	When booker B sends an HTTP request to hold seat 12
101	Then booker B is refused because the seat is held
102	And seat 12 is still reported as held for booker A
103	```
104	
105	### A sold seat is never sold again (proposed)
106	```gherkin
107	Given booker A has confirmed seat 12
108	When booker B sends an HTTP request to hold or confirm seat 12
109	Then booker B is refused because the seat is sold
110	And seat 12 is still reported as sold to booker A
111	```
112	
113	### A hold that nobody uses is released at its deadline (proposed)
114	```gherkin
115	Given seat 12 is held for booker A
116	When the deadline of the hold passes and booker A did nothing
117	Then seat 12 is reported as free
118	And booker B can hold seat 12
119	```
120	
121	### A confirmation after the deadline is refused (confirmed)
122	```gherkin
123	Given seat 12 was held for booker A and the deadline has passed
124	When booker A sends an HTTP request to confirm seat 12 with the hold reference
125	Then booker A is refused because the hold expired
126	And seat 12 is reported as free
127	```
128	
129	### The holder cancels and frees the seat at once (proposed)
130	```gherkin
131	Given seat 12 is held for booker A
132	When booker A sends an HTTP request to cancel the hold with the hold reference
133	Then seat 12 is reported as free before the deadline
134	```
135	
136	## Quint scenarios
137	
138	_Not run: no Quint model was executed for this brief._
139	
140	## Observations
141	-     Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline.
142	-     Through the HTTP API, the holder confirms their held seat before its deadline and the seat is then reported as sold to that holder.
143	-     Through the HTTP API, a second booker is refused a seat that is held or sold, and only the holder of the hold reference can confirm it, so the seat is never sold twice.
144	-     Through the HTTP API, an unconfirmed hold is released - at once when the holder cancels, and automatically when its deadline passes - and the seat is then reported as free, while a sold seat is never released.
145	
146	## Decisions
147	-     Confirmed by the human in the Request: a seat can be held for a limited time, then confirmed, cancelled or left to expire.
148	-     Confirmed by the human in the Request: safety - one seat is never sold twice.
149	-     Confirmed by the human in the Request: liveness - every hold is eventually released unless it is confirmed or cancelled.
150	-     Confirmed by the human: one fixed hold duration for all seats, set at start, default 2 minutes. A hold cannot be extended or renewed.
151	-     Confirmed by the human: the deadline is authoritative. A confirm that arrives at or after the deadline is refused with 'hold expired' and the seat is free. There is no grace window.
152	-     Confirmed by the human: holding returns a hold reference, and only the holder of that reference may confirm or cancel that hold. There are no accounts and no organizer override.
153	-     Confirmed by the human: the public port is a tiny HTTP API, not a command line interface.
154	-     Confirmed by the human: the HTTP API offers a clearly marked demo-only operation that advances the clock, so expiry is observable during a 90-minute demo.
155	-     Proposal: every HTTP response is structured data that a browser client can consume directly, not prose text.
156	-     Open: the human mentioned a thin Svelte user interface on top of the API. It is not in scope for this feature. It is undecided whether it becomes a later value, a follow-up feature or work outside nWave delivery.
157	-     Proposal: after a hold is released, the seat goes to whoever asks first, including the previous holder. There is no queue and no fairness promise.
158	-     Proposal: the seat inventory is fixed when the service starts and cannot be changed while it runs.
159	-     Assumption: a single process holds all state in memory; nothing survives a restart.
160	-     Open: no business motivation was supplied for the feature.
161	-     Open: the confirm-versus-expiry race has not been explored with generated scenarios; no Quint model was run in this turn.
162	
163	## Values
164	| Observation | Dependencies |
165	| --- | --- |
166	| Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline. |  |
167	| Through the HTTP API, the holder confirms their held seat before its deadline and the seat is then reported as sold to that holder. | Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline. |
168	| Through the HTTP API, a second booker is refused a seat that is held or sold, and only the holder of the hold reference can confirm it, so the seat is never sold twice. | Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline., Through the HTTP API, the holder confirms their held seat before its deadline and the seat is then reported as sold to that holder. |
169	| Through the HTTP API, an unconfirmed hold is released - at once when the holder cancels, and automatically when its deadline passes - and the seat is then reported as free, while a sold seat is never released. | Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline., Through the HTTP API, the holder confirms their held seat before its deadline and the seat is then reported as sold to that holder. |
170	
171	## Change intent
172	| Observation | Type | Description |
173	| --- | --- | --- |
174	| Through the HTTP API, a booker holds a free seat and the seat is then reported as held for that booker until a stated deadline. | feat | Hold a free seat for a limited time and report its holder and deadline |

12	
13	Three routes are open to a Request here, and they differ in what survives it.
14	Spine waves — the wave commands carry the gates, keep independent review and
15	source-blind EXAMINE where applicable, and leave durable authorities that
16	outlive the session; for a whole feature, evolution retains lasting facts and
17	FINALIZE closes the delivered work. Host-led DES steps — the native host invokes
18	the installed specialists; des po/design/oracle/craft/verify/integrate construct
19	facts and documents, measure actual RED/GREEN, record results or enact requested
20	native/Git effects. A public oracle exists before code. DES launches no model

22	review and no retained authority, so nothing attests the result.

25	session ends, and what a late refusal would cost, since review and
26	integration happen once per Request.

491	public driving/observation port; **liveness** proves eventual progress under
492	explicit temporal/fairness assumptions. Record each in the brief/ADR on separate
493	axes: DESIGN `PASS|BLOCKED`, runtime
494	`OBSERVED|DESIGNED_NOT_BUILT|INDETERMINATE`, and the proof/check result with its
495	actual evidence or `INDETERMINATE`. An unchecked DESIGN claim is `BLOCKED`;
496	an unexecuted checker establishes no proof. Irrelevant liveness carries a
497	concrete non-applicability reason, not a third DESIGN-axis value.
498	Bounded/synchronous execution justifies that only for liveness, never
499	safety/refinement/reachability. Omission is `BLOCKED`.

507	A formal model closes only its claim: map atoms to runtime symbols, exclusions
508	and refinement. For `RED_TO_GREEN`, unimplemented runtime is allowed only with
509	mapping/refinement obligation and declared limits. A verified mapped model may
510	close DESIGN, never runtime; without mapping it is unrefined **model-only**.
511	
512	## Counterexample discipline
513	
514	A refuted invariant, a failing property, a model-check violation, or a
515	scenario the design cannot classify is first a ROOT-CAUSE question about the
516	representation, never a patch site:
517	
518	1. Ask which type made the violating state representable. Route the
519	   diagnosis through `nw-algebraic-design-protocol` (follow the contradiction
520	   to the type or observation that causes it) and the cure through
521	   `nw-certainty-by-construction` (encode the missing distinction so the
522	   state is unrepresentable). Never add a law, guard, or ceremony on top of
523	   the unchanged representation as the first move.
524	2. A theorem that only holds conditionally is the same signal: triage its
525	   hypothesis as missing type/carrier distinction, law scope or external boundary.
526	3. An added law over an unchanged representation is a symptom patch. It may
527	   ship only with an explicit recorded justification of why the representation
528	   cannot change, in the amended durable authority.
529	   Retain each attempted concrete counterexample and its actual result; for a
530	   refuted law, name the carrier distinction, law-scope or boundary diagnosis.
531	
532	## Independent statement review — retired
533	
534	Proof/model/exhaustive artifacts verify the PROOFS, not the STATEMENTS; two
535	lanes may agree on the same misreading — that is a coherence check, never
536	corroboration. This limitation remains a DESIGN self-falsification duty, not an
537	independent delivery review. Before returning `accepted`, DESIGN attacks its own
538	observations, constructive public-oracle chain, reuse/prefactoring choices,
539	boundary/failure algebra, residual guarantees and test substrate with concrete
540	counterexamples. The delivery flow's independent quality points are the
541	acceptance-oracle review, one whole-diff implementation review, and conditional
542	source-blind EXAMINE.
543	
544	Default in every design: algebraic modeling with formal verification.
545	Missing required checkers are an installation-or-waiver decision for the human,
546	relayed by the host. Return a typed refusal naming missing tools, affected claims
547	and platform-specific install commands; do not install without authorization.
548	Only a recorded human waiver permits continuation without that proof.
549	A waived claim remains INDETERMINATE with the waiver reason, never PASS;
550	native property tests or finite checks do not silently replace it.
551	
552	For each unknown load-bearing system fact, use a bounded empirical probe and
553	record the unknown, executed fact and result. A probe resolves a discriminator,
554	never prototypes a desired answer or becomes a wave. Repeating an inconclusive
555	probe needs a changed hypothesis or useful new evidence under
556	`delivery:trustworthy-baseline-and-repair-scope`.
557	
558	Use `nw-solution-architect-formal-verification` for checker selection, bounded
559	execution, complete model/proof delivery and property-specific falsification.
560	Self-falsification may also use native property tests or finite checks, but they
561	do not replace a required formal checker. Preserve useful existing models and
562	actual host limits. Missing tooling stops the affected proof; return the typed
563	refusal to the host for the human's installation or explicit waiver choice.
564	Unrelated analysis may continue, but missing tools alone do not authorize an
565	accepted design without the required proof. Record any human waiver in
566	`decisions`, with the affected claims and reason; the proof stays `INDETERMINATE`
567	and its unchecked DESIGN claim stays `BLOCKED`, never PASS.
568	
569	Use applicable `nw-review` questions as DESIGN self-checks only (S1-S4
570	structure; selected T5-T7 time; three values); do not dispatch an independent
571	DESIGN review. They find "structural incoherence", never temporal holes; a
572	temporal gap needs a temporal/state-exploration check with the checker covering
573	that claim, TLA+/TLC when Quint is insufficient. Missing tooling follows the
574	host-relayed installation-or-waiver rule above, never a silent native-test downgrade.

576	## Handoff

578	After self-falsification, return semantic input or the caller-enforced typed
579	facts; never edit a brief, ADR, handover, or DESIGN document. An acceptance
580	finding that needs upstream rework remains with the owner of the bound
581	architecture decision. The caller may route that rework with
582	`--replace-current --input -` when it deliberately replaces the same configured
583	destination and section heading; plain `--input -` continues to refuse a
584	conflicting already-bound fact set.
585	
586	The semantic input records only current decisions and executable obligations.
587	Define purpose, common architecture and each value's delta once as catalog facts
588	so a reader unfamiliar with the Request can understand parts,
589	responsibilities and binding rules. Carry the driving port, public observations,
590	native substrate and runner argv, architectural/contract obligations, typed
591	carriers and invariants required by the downstream oracle owner. Inherit common
592	constraints without copying a second authority. The next role consumes the
593	constructed authority and role facts, not the architect's terminal reply.
594	
595	Keep complete formal model/proof bytes in external source files, cited by
596	`Model.source: {path, sha256}`; keep execution artifacts in the driven evidence
597	store under the formal-verification skill. DES persists normalized authority.
598	Keep software-observed argv, exits, outputs, traces and identities distinct from

601	When a needed assurance fact lacks a truthful carrier in the closed grammar,

604	Use an opaque diagnostic only to summarize refusal or uncertainty for a human,

**Context**

- The DISCUSS wave is done. `docs/feature/last-seat/brief.md` holds 4 ordered values. DES shows `design=absent` for all four. DES `NEXT` is `des design --value 1`. `NEXT` is advice only.
- Quint 0.33.0 and Java are installed. DESIGN needs a formal check by default, so the tools are ready. TLA+/TLC is not installed. I did not check Apalache.
- `/nw-buddy` is read-only and cannot advance a wave. The next step is `/nw-design`. I have not started it.

**Route:** Spine waves, DESIGN next. The feature must leave durable authority behind: an architecture decision, a public oracle and independent review. Working directly would keep none of these.

**Your three open items**

1. **Business motivation.**
   - DISCUSS recorded this as an open item. DESIGN cannot invent it (brief, line 160).
   - No design decision depends on it. The design goes ahead without it, with the open item and its owner (you) recorded.
2. **Svelte UI.**
   - The brief puts the UI out of scope (lines 33 and 156).
   - DESIGN keeps the API responses structured data a browser client can use directly (line 155). No UI work is designed.
   - Later work is a separate value or feature. That decision is yours.
3. **Confirm-versus-expiry race.**
   - The brief says the model was never run (lines 138 and 161). The "deadline is authoritative" rule is already confirmed (line 151).
   - Safety (no double sale) and liveness (every hold is released) are the properties to check.
   - DESIGN would write the Quint model first and run it. It would take the model's traces as input to the design. This needs no extra wave.

**Recommendation**

Run DESIGN for the whole feature, with the shared decisions first.
- The four values depend on one state model: free, held, sold, plus the clock.
- Run the Quint model before the per-value work, so traces shape the design.
- Keep the Svelte UI out of scope. Record the business motivation as an open item with you as owner.

**Options**

| Option | Consequence |
|---|---|
| A. Shared design with Quint first, then values 1–4 (recommended) | One state model for all four values. Takes slightly longer before the first value. |
| B. Design value 1 only, Quint later | Fastest start. The race and the safety claim stay unchecked, and DESIGN marks them `BLOCKED`. |
| C. Skip Quint with a recorded waiver | Quint is installed, so there is no reason to waive. The claims stay `INDETERMINATE`. |

17	
18	For native delegation, select the installed specialist in the host tool:
19	Claude `Agent(subagent_type="nw-solution-architect", prompt=...)`;
20	Codex `spawn_agent(agent_type="nw-solution-architect", message=...)`.

24	supports to select the exact installed role, with only parameters it supports.

26	facts. If the native delegation tool cannot start that exact role with its
27	declared tools ceiling, use a supported native CLI invocation or report the
28	missing capability. Never substitute a generic worker or grant extra tools.

31	|---|---|---|

34	| Acceptance oracle | `nw-acceptance-designer` | Host authors the oracle; first `des oracle --repo-root ROOT --value N --baseline REV --input -` measures current oracle/support bytes against the original source commit and records it |
35	| Implementation | `nw-software-crafter` / `nw-functional-software-crafter` | Host authors the change; `des craft --repo-root ROOT --value N --input -` measures GREEN and records it against the current oracle |
36	| Candidate review / EXAMINE | `nw-software-crafter-reviewer` / `nw-user-examiner` | `des prepare-role`, native role invocation, then `des record-role-result` |
37	| Operational facts | `nw-platform-architect` | `des devops ... --input -` constructs the supplied facts |
38	
39	For the architect, the acceptance designer and the crafter, the role's task is
40	the canonical prompt DES renders from the bound facts, its handoff and its
41	tests: run `des handoff --repo-root ROOT prompt --role ROLE [--value N]
42	--root-context FILE` (the crafter's form is `--role nw-software-crafter` or
43	`--role nw-functional-software-crafter` with `--value N`, the one the bound
44	paradigm requires: `functional` selects the functional crafter) and pass its stdout
45	verbatim as the role's task. Put your own context in FILE; never compose a
46	replacement prompt.
47	
48	### Selected independent operational review
49	
50	When the authorized DESIGN or DEVOPS task selects independent platform review, the native wave caller invokes `nw-platform-architect-reviewer` on the actual current operational authority, its bound facts, authorized scope and available observations. Use the existing native invocation form and the reviewer's declared ceiling; no producer judgment substitutes for its result.
51	
52	This is caller-owned orchestration, not a new review-task payload or a DES operation. Keep the DESIGN/`OperationalDocumentInput` constructor input closed: add no delegation, reviewer or result fields. The caller consumes the actual verdict and findings. An enabled selected review with required revisions or unresolved load-bearing evidence remains incomplete and returns its findings to the platform authority owner. A configured or human-authorized skip is reported as skipped, never approved. Constructor success does not establish review approval or authorize rollout.
53	
54	Reuse adequate authority without a new producer turn; do not add a review for a no-op when none is selected. Missing exact-role invocation capability is explicit, never a generic substitute or invented result.
55	
56	Oracle recorder input is `{"structured_output":{"outcome":"accepted","diagnostic":"..."}}`.
57	Craft additionally requires `"blocked_by":null` for accepted results; a
58	nonaccepted result names `product`, `design`, or `oracle`. These envelopes
59	record host work; they do not author files or replace actual RED/GREEN.
60	
61	Choose the original pre-implementation commit for `--baseline REV`, not HEAD
62	when HEAD already includes the fix. Measurement uses the existing disposable
63	candidate checkout and preserves the working tree and index. The single
64	resolver selects explicit baseline, then a Request base when supplied, then the
65	recorded witness baseline. Request base production/wiring is not yet implemented
66	here. Later corrections can omit the flag and reuse the recorded source; a
67	differing explicit baseline wins and is recorded. `ORACLE-BASELINE` reports the
68	resolved SHA and source. With no source, `OracleBaselineMissing` refuses with
69	WHAT/WHY/HOW; supply `--baseline <original source commit>` rather than guessing HEAD.
70	
71	Baseline Python measurements require an armed interpreter-start receipt before
72	admitting any verdict. Missing or refused isolation evidence is
73	`OracleProbeUnavailable` (Indeterminate), never RED/GREEN; use a Python
74	invocation that loads site and honours PYTHONPATH, without `-I`, `-E` or `-S`.
75	Declared dependencies in shared `.venv` remain available. The guard is not a
76	filesystem sandbox or complete hostile-loader certification: a Python descendant
77	that suppresses startup or erases its environment is not detected when its
78	parent invocation supplies admissible receipts or is non-Python. The acceptance
79	designer owns that unknown and should declare the Python oracle directly.
80	
81	For an applicable bound prefactoring decision, the host records actual native
82	preservation runs with `des craft --repo-root ROOT --value N
83	--prefactoring-phase before-move` and, after only the declared movement,
84	`--prefactoring-phase after-move-before-behavior`. These measure preservation
85	without `--input`; they neither invoke the crafter nor replace the ordinary
86	feature RED/GREEN record. The advisory `NEXT` names the owed phase before
87	`des oracle` and a phase refusal retries as that phase; DES executes neither.
88	For the first oracle measurement, supply `--baseline <original source commit>`;
89	subsequent corrections reuse its recorded baseline unless explicitly overridden.
90	Keep the intermediate production and unchanged
91	oracle/support/runtime identities required by `nw-code-craftsmanship`.
92	
93	For selected-revision recovery, explicitly select the acceptance designer:
94	`des prepare-role --repo-root ROOT --role acceptance-designer --task selected-revision-recovery --value N --finding -`.
95	Pass its exact sealed `INPUT`, required skills and output schema to the native
96	role. Record the host envelope with `des record-role-result --repo-root ROOT
97	--role acceptance-designer --task selected-revision-recovery --value N
98	--prepared-input INPUT --provider {claude,codex} --model MODEL --session-id SESSION
99	--input -` (no candidate). An accepted result includes the complete
100	`distill_document` v2. Pass the reported document bytes unchanged to
101	`des distill --repo-root ROOT --replace-current --input -` only if you choose
102	that correction. DES does not retry or select a successor.
103	
104	If the document does not answer the finding, prepare a corrected finding.
105	Each distinct finding seals a distinct INPUT; invoke the new packet rather
106	than replaying an obsolete packet or rebuilding the handover.
107	
108	## Constructors
109	
110	`des discuss|po|design|distill|devops ... --input -` construct documents from host-supplied semantic facts. They invoke no role. Configuration retains explicit provider/model/effort facts for the native host where supported; it is not a DES executor or fallback policy.
111	Constructing returned facts never replaces invoking the role: a caller that
112	authors the facts itself has skipped the specialist. Suitable existing durable
113	authority may be reused as already allowed; no role turn is added for a no-op.
114	
115	## Scope
116	
117	DISCUSS, PO and DEVOPS require exactly one of `--project`, `--epic ID`, `--feature ID`, `--slice FEATURE_ID SLICE_ID`. DESIGN and DISTILL inherit the persisted scope. Output paths come from configuration and the constructor's report; hardcode none.
118	
119	Resolve effective configured destinations, bound section headings, repository
120	naming/discovery conventions and scope once and pass them to all affected roles.
121	Include the original Request, authorized human exclusions/amendments and their
122	provenance in ordinary role/review handoffs; producer-only scope reduction is
123	not authorization. Do not ask the human to repeat a known configuration rule.
124	EXAMINE gets only the authorized behavioral contract within its source-blind
125	boundary, never architecture, oracle, selectors or producer classifications.
126	
127	Supply canonical constructor grammar, exact task and actual tool ceiling. A
128	Read-only PO cannot run `des ... --describe-input`: the host retrieves and passes
129	the grammar and immutable supplied facts, then constructs the role's returned
130	manifest unchanged. StructuredOutput is available only if the native host
131	actually supports it. Consume all field/chunk views and authenticate their
132	reconstruction against the independently retained `INPUT-SHA256`, not a digest
133	inside the mutable views manifest. Record against the sealed original `INPUT`.
134	Truncated diff prose is not complete review. Caller-supplied free-text scope
135	context stays on the ordinary reviewer side; EXAMINE uses only its permitted
136	behavioral contract and public observations.
137	Reference `nw-typesafe-system-one` for role-owned unchanged-request relay;
138	a skill mention is not evidence of client/caller-exchange capability.
139	
140	## Reviewer and examiner boundaries
141	
142	For DISTILL before-code alignment, MUST read
143	`~/.claude/skills/nw-at-completeness-check/SKILL.md`. When the original value,
144	selected contract, and prior adequate alignment are unchanged with no new
145	finding, reuse it without another preimplementation assessment or ATD review.
146	Only for new, changed, or unresolved semantics, invoke the installed
147	`nw-user-examiner` natively with an explicit preimplementation assessment task
148	and only the original Request plus the same selected behavioral contract bytes
149	supplied to ATD. Keep its tools empty apart from structured output; provide
150	neither oracle/production source nor test-derived expectations. Return its
151	independent expectations to the existing ATD reviewer for the shared review.
152	An alignment verdict concerns observation feasibility and ambiguity, not runtime
153	acceptance; unavailable implementation evidence is not a failure of alignment.
154	
155	The preimplementation acceptance reviewer receives the dedicated host-supplied
156	packet defined by `nw-at-completeness-check`, including oracle/support evidence
157	and authorized scope. A candidate reviewer `prepare-role` packet is not that
158	packet and must not be advertised as available before implementation.
159	
160	Current DES examiner preparation requires a verified candidate. It projects the
161	selected DISTILL acceptance as source-blind ordered criterion id, stimulus,
162	expected observation, revision identity, and locator-withholding markers. Its
163	inputs are content-addressed revisions; corrected observations retain prior
164	inputs and results. It cannot serve a preimplementation assessment because no
165	verified candidate exists yet: use the native installed examiner for that task.
166	For final EXAMINE, use the prepared selected-acceptance projection; report a gap
167	only when that actual projection is unavailable, never by treating the broad
168	Request as equivalent. Invent no CLI flag, replace no sealed evidence, and make
169	no production edit just to obtain a new candidate. DES remains the durable
170	document writer; the LLM selects invocations.
171	
172	Check the selected role's `tools` declaration. A tools-empty role, including
173	`nw-user-examiner`, cannot read paths: supply its permitted evidence bytes.
174	For EXAMINE, the caller first captures selected public stimuli, responses and
175	state snapshots for the verified candidate, then runs
176	`des prepare-role --repo-root ROOT --role examiner --candidate SHA --observations PATH`.
177	DES seals the caller-supplied packet after grammar, candidate, size and
178	known-path checks. It does not capture or select events, verify the packet's
179	declared substrate, or judge the observations. Use the exact `INPUT` it prints.
180	Successful preparation also prints `ROLE-ID` and `RESULT-SCHEMA` (compact JSON
181	Schema). Supply that exact schema to native structured output: reviewer defect
182	values are packet-bound, examiner output is payload-free, and recovery uses its
183	closed semantic-task schema. Wrap the returned object as `{"structured_output":
184	RESULT_OBJECT}` for `record-role-result`; preserve actual host provenance.
185	
186	A tools-empty examiner must receive the permitted packet bytes in a fresh
187	source-blind context, not repository access or a path it cannot read. On the
188	current Claude host, native Agent cannot start a tools-empty role; use the
189	native CLI with `--agent nw-user-examiner --tools '' --allowedTools
190	StructuredOutput --json-schema SCHEMA`, supplying its mandatory skills,
191	bound packet and required output schema. Keep production/oracle sources
192	unmounted and absent from the prompt. Do not add Read to repair this limit.
193	The code reviewer retains its normal declared Read capability.
194	
195	Bind each reviewer or examiner result to its exact content-addressed input revision:
196	
197	```bash
198	printf '%s' "$RESULT" | des record-role-result --repo-root ROOT --role examiner \
199	  --candidate SHA --provider {claude,codex} --model MODEL --session-id SESSION \
200	  --input - --prepared-input INPUT
201	```
202	
203	`--prepared-input` selects the precise prepared revision rather than guessing
204	the newest packet; it is required for reviewer, examiner and recovery recording.
205	The examiner reads the packet, its provenance and any native-detail withholding
206	markers; it returns `INDETERMINATE` for behavior that lacks an observation. The
207	reviewer is unaffected and receives its existing full evidence. The examiner
208	receives observations and the original value/Request, never production source
209	or oracle source. An oracle reviewer receives the oracle bytes; a code reviewer
210	with `Read` can inspect the candidate at its supplied paths. Absent evidence is
211	`INDETERMINATE`; adding tools is not the repair.
212	
213	## Currentness and candidate lifecycle
214	
215	Read current state before choosing the next host action. Reuse unchanged adequate
216	semantic authority/alignment selectively by value and consumed prerequisites;
217	native remeasurement is not automatic reauthoring or transitive role replay.
218	Source identity alone is insufficient when contract/oracle/runtime changed.
219	Distinguish missing facts, graph drift, owned/upstream bytes drift and destination
220	drift and route their concrete causes to the owner. A step's Success does not
221	close the authorized Request; continue until real obligations and integration
222	are current, stopping for a genuine human checkpoint/choice, not a recoverable
223	mechanical fact.
224	
225	Agree commit/staging/install lifecycle before craft. Commits carry only owned
226	source/test/support/authority: never stage, force-add or per-step WIP-commit
227	`.nwave/des/**`. Retain runtime state in the lane worktree, not Git history;
228	leave historical runtime commits untouched. Retain actual before/after revisions
229	and preserve candidate snapshots/evidence when disposable execution workspaces
230	are removed. Owned source/test/support/authority edits after VERIFY
231	need a new candidate/current independent review; never restamp an old approval.
232	Archived graphs remain historical, not automatically reactivated. Destination CAS,
233	foreign bytes and staging are preserved; no reset recipe or cleanup of user WIP.
234	Probes use invocation-local disposable scope or declared nonowned output, retain
235	their receipt and remove only their own files. Preflight actual native processes,
236	ports, writable build/temp/cache and separate space/inode requirements; provider
237	auth/quota/timeout, machine/setup failure and product rejection stay distinct.
238	
239	Reuse native execution evidence only when source, oracle/supports, argv/cwd,
240	environment/toolchain/substrate, consumed contracts and purpose remain identical
241	and the assurance permits it. Independent review and stress have distinct
242	purposes; neither is a producer cache. Require authentic native attribution of
243	assertion versus setup/build/import failure where observable, otherwise
244	INDETERMINATE. Missing counts/reporters or unknown code-fact radius never become
245	zero. Accounting uses actual timeline overlap, root/child session dedup and
246	returned provider/Jev usage; interrupted or missing cost is unknown, not zero.
247	
248	## Waiting
249	
250	For native model subagents, use host completion notifications or their actual
251	completion handle. For a long-running native CLI/process, retain and resume its
252	real process handle until terminal output arrives. Never use fixed sleeps,
253	silence, or an invented notification as evidence of completion; never launch a
254	duplicate invocation while the first remains active.
255	
256	## Human interaction
257	
258	Offer interaction per `nw-human-collaboration`; honor an already chosen mode.
259

Only for new, changed, or unresolved semantics, invoke the installed
`nw-user-examiner` natively with an explicit preimplementation assessment task
and only the original Request plus the same selected behavioral contract bytes
supplied to ATD. Keep its tools empty apart from structured output; provide
neither oracle/production source nor test-derived expectations. Return its
independent expectations to the existing ATD reviewer for the shared review.
An alignment verdict concerns observation feasibility and ambiguity, not runtime
acceptance; unavailable implementation evidence is not a failure of alignment.

The preimplementation acceptance reviewer receives the dedicated host-supplied
packet defined by `nw-at-completeness-check`, including oracle/support evidence
and authorized scope. A candidate reviewer `prepare-role` packet is not that
packet and must not be advertised as available before implementation.

Current DES examiner preparation requires a verified candidate. It projects the
selected DISTILL acceptance as source-blind ordered criterion id, stimulus,
expected observation, revision identity, and locator-withholding markers. Its
inputs are content-addressed revisions; corrected observations retain prior
inputs and results. It cannot serve a preimplementation assessment because no
verified candidate exists yet: use the native installed examiner for that task.
For final EXAMINE, use the prepared selected-acceptance projection; report a gap
only when that actual projection is unavailable, never by treating the broad
Request as equivalent. Invent no CLI flag, replace no sealed evidence, and make
no production edit just to obtain a new candidate. DES remains the durable
document writer; the LLM selects invocations.

Check the selected role's `tools` declaration. A tools-empty role, including
`nw-user-examiner`, cannot read paths: supply its permitted evidence bytes.
For EXAMINE, the caller first captures selected public stimuli, responses and
state snapshots for the verified candidate, then runs
`des prepare-role --repo-root ROOT --role examiner --candidate SHA --observations PATH`.
DES seals the caller-supplied packet after grammar, candidate, size and
known-path checks. It does not capture or select events, verify the packet's
declared substrate, or judge the observations. Use the exact `INPUT` it prints.
Successful preparation also prints `ROLE-ID` and `RESULT-SCHEMA` (compact JSON
Schema). Supply that exact schema to native structured output: reviewer defect
values are packet-bound, examiner output is payload-free, and recovery uses its
closed semantic-task schema. Wrap the returned object as `{"structured_output":
RESULT_OBJECT}` for `record-role-result`; preserve actual host provenance.

A tools-empty examiner must receive the permitted packet bytes in a fresh
source-blind context, not repository access or a path it cannot read. On the
current Claude host, native Agent cannot start a tools-empty role; use the
native CLI with `--agent nw-user-examiner --tools '' --allowedTools
StructuredOutput --json-schema SCHEMA`, supplying its mandatory skills,
bound packet and required output schema. Keep production/oracle sources
unmounted and absent from the prompt. Do not add Read to repair this limit.
The code reviewer retains its normal declared Read capability.

Bind each reviewer or examiner result to its exact content-addressed input revision:

```bash
printf '%s' "$RESULT" | des record-role-result --repo-root ROOT --role examiner \
  --candidate SHA --provider {claude,codex} --model MODEL --session-id SESSION \
  --input - --prepared-input INPUT
```

`--prepared-input` selects the precise prepared revision rather than guessing
the newest packet; it is required for reviewer, examiner and recovery recording.
The examiner reads the packet, its provenance and any native-detail withholding
markers; it returns `INDETERMINATE` for behavior that lacks an observation. The
reviewer is unaffected and receives its existing full evidence. The examiner
receives observations and the original value/Request, never production source
or oracle source. An oracle reviewer receives the oracle bytes; a code reviewer
with `Read` can inspect the candidate at its supplied paths. Absent evidence is
`INDETERMINATE`; adding tools is not the repair.

## Currentness and candidate lifecycle

Read current state before choosing the next host action. Reuse unchanged adequate
semantic authority/alignment selectively by value and consumed prerequisites;
native remeasurement is not automatic reauthoring or transitive role replay.
Source identity alone is insufficient when contract/oracle/runtime changed.
Distinguish missing facts, graph drift, owned/upstream bytes drift and destination
drift and route their concrete causes to the owner. A step's Success does not
close the authorized Request; continue until real obligations and integration
are current, stopping for a genuine human checkpoint/choice, not a recoverable
mechanical fact.

Agree commit/staging/install lifecycle before craft. Commits carry only owned
source/test/support/authority: never stage, force-add or per-step WIP-commit
`.nwave/des/**`. Retain runtime state in the lane worktree, not Git history;
leave historical runtime commits untouched. Retain actual before/after revisions
and preserve candidate snapshots/evidence when disposable execution workspaces
are removed. Owned source/test/support/authority edits after VERIFY
need a new candidate/current independent review; never restamp an old approval.
Archived graphs remain historical, not automatically reactivated. Destination CAS,
foreign bytes and staging are preserved; no reset recipe or cleanup of user WIP.
Probes use invocation-local disposable scope or declared nonowned output, retain
their receipt and remove only their own files. Preflight actual native processes,
ports, writable build/temp/cache and separate space/inode requirements; provider
auth/quota/timeout, machine/setup failure and product rejection stay distinct.

Reuse native execution evidence only when source, oracle/supports, argv/cwd,
environment/toolchain/substrate, consumed contracts and purpose remain identical
and the assurance permits it. Independent review and stress have distinct
purposes; neither is a producer cache. Require authentic native attribution of
assertion versus setup/build/import failure where observable, otherwise
INDETERMINATE. Missing counts/reporters or unknown code-fact radius never become
zero. Accounting uses actual timeline overlap, root/child session dedup and
returned provider/Jev usage; interrupted or missing cost is unknown, not zero.

## Waiting

For native model subagents, use host completion notifications or their actual
completion handle. For a long-running native CLI/process, retain and resume its
real process handle until terminal output arrives. Never use fixed sleeps,
silence, or an invented notification as evidence of completion; never launch a
duplicate invocation while the first remains active.

## Human interaction

Offer interaction per `nw-human-collaboration`; honor an already chosen mode.

232	refinement and preservation obligations explicit. Render relevant traces into

238	- `nw-algebraic-design-protocol` — observations, equality and public terms.
239	- `nw-certainty-by-construction` — local construction boundary.
240	- `nw-formal-verification-tlaplus` — TLA+/TLC modeling heuristics.
241

243	
244	Do these items have current model/artifact and executed-check evidence where
245	required, rather than presence, declarations or recollection? If not, retain
246	each affected limitation in the supported semantic carrier and withhold only
247	the unsupported claim; obtain missing authorized evidence where possible.
248	
249	- [ ] Tool availability was executed, not asserted.
250	- [ ] An available selected checker ran on the actual model/proof (own or host
251	  receipt); substitute evidence is labelled separately.
252	- [ ] The selected tool and property match local or state-transition trigger.
253	- [ ] A new state model uses Quint, or the authority records why direct TLA+ is required.
254	- [ ] Probe and any installation offer match the actual host platform.
255	- [ ] The authority names mapping, exclusions, mapping/refinement obligation
256	  and declared limits; it never calls a model result runtime coverage.
257	- [ ] A Quint verification records `.qnt`, backend/configuration, properties,
258	  bounds, literal argv, exit status and result; simulation is labelled separately.
259	- [ ] A TLA run records `.tla`, `.cfg`, literal TLC argv, exit status and result.
260	- [ ] Non-functional model assumptions and required runtime measurements are explicit.
261	- [ ] A missing checker returned a typed refusal with tools, affected claims,
262	  platform-specific installation commands and a host-relayed human waiver option.
263	- [ ] Any continuation without a required proof has a recorded human waiver;
264	  affected claims retain `INDETERMINATE` and the waiver reason, never PASS.
265	
266	Reference: https://quint.sh/docs/quint#command-verify

   mechanism/protocol atomicity, or `QUESTION/NEEDS_INPUT`.
5. **Offer installation or human waiver** — a missing needed checker stops
   that proof, not the algebraic modeling requirement. Return a typed refusal
   through the caller's existing enforced schema, naming the missing tools,
   affected claims, observed platform, and two human choices: install the tools
   with exact platform-specific commands, or explicitly waive that verification.
   As a subagent, return this offer to the host; the host relays it to the human.
   Do not ask the human yourself, auto-download a backend, install without
   authorization, silently downgrade to native tests, claim PASS or fake a run.
   Only a recorded human waiver permits continuation without that proof.
   Keep the explicit waiver evidence external; reference only its current
   affected claim and reason through FactRefs. The proof stays `INDETERMINATE`.
   A refusal to install is not itself a waiver. An unknown platform/package
   manager requires a bounded host observation, not an invented install command.
   Provide only the dependencies actually needed by the selected claims.
   Examples to adapt after observing the platform and available tools:

   | Needed tool | Installation offer (host relays; never execute without consent) |
   |---|---|
   | Quint with Node.js/npm available | `npm install -g @informalsystems/quint` |
   | Java/Agda on observed Arch Linux | `sudo pacman -S jre-openjdk agda` (select only missing packages) |
   | Direct TLC with Java available | `curl -fL --output <outside-repo>/tla2tools.jar https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/latest/download/tla2tools.jar` |

   Keep equations, observations and vacuity checks while waiting for the host's
   decision; missing tools do not authorize an accepted proof-less design.
   Return only the caller's supported semantic carrier or typed diagnostic.
   If its schema cannot express the limitation, return its representation-gap
   outcome; never invent fields, a new schema or a false proof.

## Serial execution and bound growth

Run checkers one at a time: shared backend resources can collide. Use the
execution host's portable process deadline, not an assumed shell `timeout`.
Budget each verification/TLC run at 180 seconds unless current authority states
a different explicit budget; retain the limit with the result.
Start at the smallest instance that reaches the seam: two processes and the
fewest relevant steps for a concurrent claim, or the corresponding minimal
local instance. Increase only after the previous run finishes within budget:
two processes -> three -> failures -> liveness. Record completed bounds and
where growth stops. A timed-out bound is `INDETERMINATE`; do not repeat it
unchanged. Smaller focused slices may resolve different claims, never stand in
for the timed-out property at its promised scope.

## Liveness and fairness

Use a finite TLC slice with the state needed by the temporal property and its
actions; remove ghost histories and unbounded counters only when the projection
preserves those behaviors. State the projection limits. Retain its complete
text just as for the safety model.

Express assumed fairness as a temporal formula, for example
`weakFair(action, vars)` or `strongFair(action, vars)`, with its actual action
and variables. Explain whose scheduling/progress obligation it assumes.
For a Quint model, the native form is:

```text
quint verify MODEL.qnt --init=init --step=step --temporal=PROPERTY --backend tlc
```

Keep distinct executed runs and receipts for:

| Run | Required observation |
|---|---|
| Progress property without fairness | Counterexample showing the admitted stuttering/do-nothing behavior |
| Property under declared fairness | Passing check on that finite scope |
| Mutant removing progress or release, under the same fairness | Counterexample refuting that progress guarantee |

Keep the raw traces, not only summaries. If the no-fairness claim already holds,
explain the model's actual progress guarantee rather than invent stuttering.
If the declared protocol has no truthful matching evidence, its liveness DESIGN
axis stays `BLOCKED`; retain runtime and proof results independently.
Finite-state checking proves neither unbounded runtime scheduling nor elapsed
time; name those remaining obligations and owners.

## Delivery and evidence locators

The normalized DESIGN manifest carries current claim FactRefs, source locators
and run ids only. Keep complete model/proof files at their intended committed
repository-relative paths and cite `Model.source: {path, sha256}`. The host owns
authority publication. Record actual checker/probe executions only with
`des handoff run` and `des handoff record` in the driven receipt store; use their
public help for exact argv. Never invent a receipt command or submit a receipts
section, inline model text, history/provenance/supersession narration or receipt
prose inside facts/decisions. Independent review and EXAMINE judge author-text
compliance; there is no semantic classifier or substring gate.

| Evidence | Required external content |
|---|---|
| Model/proof and temporal slice | Complete unedited file with line breaks; language, sha256 and committed source path |
| Checker run | Actual argv, tool version, backend/configuration, properties, bounds or seed, exit, result and raw outputs/traces |
| Mutant | Exact changed behavior, model identity, property it falsifies and its counterexample/rejection receipt |
| Refinement | Each action/step's file, symbol and mechanism making it atomic, or the real seam splitting it; unmapped steps explicitly model-only |

A hash, scratch file, intended command or successful version probe is not model
delivery or verification. Claim property coverage only for checks the actual
run exercised; an aggregate green result does not supply missing law receipts.
Keep observed process facts separate from declared checks and interpretation.
Replay evidence retains its original revision; it is not a newly observed run.
When no callable capability can execute or persist the required evidence,
return that bounded limitation to the host and leave the claim `INDETERMINATE`.

For native `des handoff check`, `render`, `summary` and `prompt`, use the bound
graph's FactCatalog. Detached FILE input must explicitly cite schema-2 DESIGN
manifest files as `catalog: [{path, sha256}]`; digests and merged definitions
must agree. Do not inline a replacement catalog into producer
`--architect-handoff FILE` input: its context is the constructing manifest plus
bound shared facts. Missing detached context refuses render/summary/prompt with
`ArchitectHandoffCatalogUnavailable`; check runs structural rules while
text/reference/template/trace-dependent rules remain UNRUN. Neither missing
context nor an unresolved FactRef is a passing formal check.


## Non-functional requirements and human review

Name the actor, observation, operating conditions, units and threshold before
modeling a non-functional requirement. Use explicit time, resource and fault
assumptions: state-transition count is not elapsed time. Separate real failure
from detected failure, and stated capacity from measured throughput. Model
checking can establish a property of those assumptions; actual latency,
throughput, recovery and availability still need their relevant runtime tests.
Do not claim a production percentile or service level from model exploration.

Reuse the PO's behavioral core where available, then make architectural
refinement and preservation obligations explicit. Render relevant traces into
domain-language scenarios for human review using `nw-po-scenario-exploration`;
the human need not read Quint or TLA+. Keep raw traces and model identity.

- `nw-algebraic-design-protocol` — observations, equality and public terms.
- `nw-certainty-by-construction` — local construction boundary.
- `nw-formal-verification-tlaplus` — TLA+/TLC modeling heuristics.

## Verification

Do these items have current model/artifact and executed-check evidence where
required, rather than presence, declarations or recollection? If not, retain
each affected limitation in the supported semantic carrier and withhold only
the unsupported claim; obtain missing authorized evidence where possible.

- [ ] Tool availability was executed, not asserted.
- [ ] An available selected checker ran on the actual model/proof (own or host

- [ ] The selected tool and property match local or state-transition trigger.
- [ ] A new state model uses Quint, or the authority records why direct TLA+ is required.
- [ ] Probe and any installation offer match the actual host platform.
- [ ] The authority names mapping, exclusions, mapping/refinement obligation

- [ ] A Quint verification records `.qnt`, backend/configuration, properties,

- [ ] A TLA run records `.tla`, `.cfg`, literal TLC argv, exit status and result.
- [ ] Non-functional model assumptions and required runtime measurements are explicit.
- [ ] A missing checker returned a typed refusal with tools, affected claims,
  platform-specific installation commands and a host-relayed human waiver option.
- [ ] Any continuation without a required proof has a recorded human waiver;
  affected claims retain `INDETERMINATE` and the waiver reason, never PASS.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort.
